whatItIs.text: A crisp, 95%-water fruit of a climbing vine, botanically a pepo; slicing, pickling, and seedless are the three main types.

historyNote.text: Cucumbers come from Asia, from India across to northern Thailand; they have been cultivated for at least 3,000 years — the emperor Tiberius reportedly ate them year-round — and the Spanish carried them to the Americas by 1494.

howToChoose.text: Choose firm, evenly dark cucumbers without wrinkles or soft ends; larger ones can carry more seeds and bitterness.

storage.text: Refrigerate in the crisper, loosely wrapped, and keep away from the coldest shelf, which can pit them. The rulebook has the details.

foodSafetyRef.note: shelf-life guidance lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Soft cucumbers make quick pickles, raita, or chilled soup; peel and deseed if the skin has toughened.

substitutions.note: similar crunch and mildness; slightly sweeter, great in salads
